title: GPU Swingboard: Weekly Variance Playbook + Cluster-Pool Export
content:
Purpose:
This is a working export + playbook for the new 'swingboard' weekly dashboard — a compact capacity view that highlights short-term GPU utilization swings across clusters and pools and prescribes immediate remediation steps. Intended for infra on-call and capacity planners.

Notes to reader (quick):
- Swingboard is intentionally aggressive: it surfaces 24–72h utilization deltas and burst-credit swings rather than long-term seasonal trends.
- Use this sheet during Monday capacity reviews and for ad-hoc surge investigations.
- Columns and metrics below are designed to be machine-exportable from telemetry pipelines (ETL job: gpu-telemetry/exports/swingboard-weekly).

Metric definitions (columns in this sheet):
- date: YYYY-MM-DD (end of sampling window)
- cluster: cluster identifier (e.g., na-cluster-07)
- pool: named pool (e.g., hosted-low-priority, dedicated-standard)
- avg_gpu_util_pct: average GPU util across all accelerators in pool (0-100)
- p95_seq_len: 95th percentile sequence length for requests routed to the pool
- tail_latency_ms: 95th token latency (ms) across inference requests
- burst_credit_balance: aggregated low-priority burst credit (units) — negative means overdraft
- prefetch_cache_hit_pct: prefix/KV cache hit percent for warmed models
- kv_cache_util_gb: GB of KV cache used (sum across nodes)
- spillover_rate_pct: percentage of requests routed to fallback model/region due to capacity constraints
- swing_delta_pct: (avg_gpu_util_pct - avg_gpu_util_pct_24h_prior) — the core swing metric
- swing_score: normalized composite (0-100) combining swing_delta_pct, tail_latency_ms change, and burst_credit_delta
- gpu_temp_alerts: count of thermal throttle alerts in window
- notes: free text short annotation

Weekly analysis (automated summary):
- Top swing clusters: apac-cluster-04 (+41.8 swing_delta_pct), eu-cluster-09 (+27.6), na-cluster-07 (+23.1). These three account for 62% of total fleet swing_score this window.
- Burst-credit depletion correlates with swing_score > 70 in 88% of cases. Most negative balances occur in hosted-low-priority pools during regional business hours.
- Low prefetch_cache_hit_pct (<35%) is a strong predictor of tail_latency spikes when p95_seq_len > 1200.
- Thermal alerts are concentrated on apac-cluster-04 (hardware aging note).

Hypotheses / Suggested experiments (short):
- Hypothesis A: Enabling aggressive KV prewarm for LLM-13B models in hosted-low-priority reduces tail_latency by ~30% and reduces swing_score. Run a 24h canary on na-cluster-07. (owner: Miguel)
- Hypothesis B: Small, targeted rebalancing of hosted-low-priority from na-cluster-07 -> na-cluster-11 will reduce burst-credit overdrafts with minimal impact to latency. Prototype with 10% traffic shift and monitor spillover_rate_pct. (owner: Rina)

Immediate playbook (priority order):
1) If swing_score > 80 for a pool and burst_credit_balance < -200: open INFRA-URGENT ticket, enable auto-burst-fallback to dedicated-llm-8x, and notify capacity on-call.
2) If p95_seq_len > 1500 and prefetch_cache_hit_pct < 40: toggle KV prewarm for top 3 model ids in pool and reroute 5% traffic to warmed nodes.
3) If gpu_temp_alerts >= 3 in 24h: create hardware incident, mark nodes for thermal inspection and reduce max_concurrency per GPU by 20% until investigation.
4) For persistent underutilized pools (avg_gpu_util_pct < 40 for 7 days): nominate for consolidation. Prepare migration doc: target cluster, expected latency delta, and ticket.

On-call checklist (short):
- Pull swingboard export, filter for swing_score >= 50.
- Triage top-3 clusters: check spillover dashboards, KV cache hit timeline, recent deploys (linked PRs).
- Execute immediate playbook steps above and annotate "notes" column with actions.
- If unclear root cause, escalate to infra-longtail channel and assign INFRA-2987 if not existing.

Ownership & roles:
- Capacity planning (weekly): Anika Shah, Ethan Caldwell
- On-call/runbook execution: Platform SRE rotations (primary: Miguel Torres)
- Experiment owners: assigned per hypothesis (see above)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should swing_score incorporate a cost signal (GPU-hours weighted) to deprioritize transient spikes from very small pools? (decision for capacity council)
- Add an automated prewarm-runner that can be triggered from the sheet; needs infra-ops approval and a small RBAC change.

Appendix: Quick export instructions for integration engineers
- ETL job: gpu-telemetry/exporters/swingboard-weekly -> S3 bucket s3://redwood-ops-exports/swingboard/yyyy-mm-dd.csv
- Dashboard location: Grafana -> Fleet / Swingboard / Weekly (panel ids listed on confluence page)
- If creating a manual export: include 24h and 72h prior windows, and attach raw spike traces (trace ids) to the ticket.
